1. (Currently amended) A method of providing advertisements in a traffic message comprising: - obtaining traffic data having a traffic condition of a location description on a road network __using a traffic data processing system__; - assessing a location reference code associated with the location description assigned by a traffic message supplier __using the traffic data processing system__; - assessing an advertising reference code associated with the location reference code __using the traffic data processing system__; - determining whether the advertising reference code is present __using the traffic data processing system__.

2. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 1 is implemented at server side of a traffic service network.

3. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 1 further comprising: - generating a traffic message having the location reference code when the advertising reference code is not present.

4. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 1 further comprising: - providing the traffic message for broadcast to navigation systems.

5. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 4, wherein the traffic message is broadcast using any one or more selected from a group of Radio Data System (RDS), Traffic Message Channel (TMC), Radio Data System-Traffic Message Channel (RDS-TMC), Vehicle Information and Communication System, digital radio, satellite radio, mobile Internet, mobile paging, and General Packet Radio Services/Global System for Mobile (GPRS/GSM) phone networks.

6. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 1 further comprising, prior to assessing an advertising reference code associated with the location reference code: - determining whether the traffic message is a message of every predefined number of messages for broadcast; and - generating a traffic message having the location reference code when the traffic message is a message of every predefined number of messages for broadcast.

7. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 1, wherein the predefined number of messages is based, at least in part, on any one or more selected from a group of a predefined time duration, every 10th message, every 50th message, every 100th message, a range of every 10th to 25th message, a range of every 50th to 65th message, and a range of every 100th to 150th message.

8. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 1, wherein the traffic message uses any one or more selected from a group of an Alert-C protocol, Alert-Plus protocol, packet-based protocol, and Vehicle Information and Communication System message protocol.

9. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 1, wherein the location reference code comprises any one or more selected from a group of a geographic location, a point of interest, a local location of a geographic location.

10. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 1, wherein the advertising reference code comprises any one or more selected from a group of resource codes representing at least a portion of an advertisement and a substantially unique code identifying at least a portion of an advertisement stored on a recipient device of the traffic message.

11. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 1, wherein assessing an advertising reference code associated with the location reference code further comprises: - assessing a current time; - assessing the advertising reference code based, at least in part, on the current time.

12. (Previously presented) A computer-readable medium having executable instructions stored thereon in accordance with the method of Claim 1.

13. (Previously presented) An apparatus having executable instructions stored thereon in accordance with the method of Claim 1.

14. (Currently amended) A method of providing advertisement messages using location reference codes comprising: - assessing a location reference code of a location description __using an advertisement processing system__; - assessing an advertising reference code associated with the location reference code __using the advertisement processing system__; - generating an advertising message having the advertising reference code __using the advertisement processing system__; and - providing the advertising message for broadcast to navigation systems __using the advertisement processing system__.

15. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 14 is implemented at server side of a traffic service network.

16. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 14, wherein the advertising messages are sent every predefined number of messages for broadcast.

17. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 16, wherein the predefined number of messages is based, at least in part, on any one or more selected from a group of a predefined time duration, every 10th message, every 50th message, every 100th message, a range of every 10th to 25th message, a range of every 50th to 65th message, and a range of every 100th to 150th message.

18. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 14, wherein the advertising message is broadcast using any one or more selected from a group of Radio Data System (RDS), Traffic Message Channel (TMC), Radio Data System-Traffic Message Channel (RDS-TMC), Vehicle Information and Communication System, digital radio, satellite radio, mobile Internet, mobile paging, and General Packet Radio Services/Global System for Mobile (GPRS/GSM) phone networks.

19. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 14, wherein the traffic message uses any one or more selected from a group of an Alert-C protocol, Alert-Plus protocol, packet-based protocol, and Vehicle Information and Communication System message protocol.

20. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 14, wherein the location reference code comprises any one or more selected from a group of a geographic location, a point of interest, a local location of a geographic location.

21. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 14, wherein the advertising reference code comprises any one or more selected from a group of resource codes representing at least a portion of an advertisement and a substantially unique code identifying at least a portion of an advertisement stored on a recipient device of the advertising message.

22. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 14, wherein assessing an advertising reference code associated with the location reference code further comprises: - assessing a current time; - assessing the advertising reference code based, at least in part, on the current time.

23. (Previously presented) A computer-readable medium having executable instructions stored thereon in accordance with the method of Claim 14.

24. (Previously presented) An apparatus having executable instructions stored thereon in accordance with the method of Claim 14.

25. (Currently amended) A method of providing advertisements comprising: - generating a message having an advertising reference code __using an advertisement generation system__; and - providing the message for broadcast to navigation systems __using the advertisement generation system__, wherein the advertising reference code comprises a substantially unique code that identifies at least a portion of an advertisement stored and displayed on a recipient device of the message.

26. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 25 is implemented at server side of a traffic service network.

27. (Currently amended) A method of providing advertisements via a traffic channel comprising: - generating a message having advertisements __using a message generation system__; and - serially transmitting the message for broadcast to navigation systems via the traffic channel __using the message generation system__.

28. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 27 is implemented at server side of a traffic service network.

29. (Currently amended) A method of providing advertisements using location reference codes comprising: - receiving a message from a traffic supplier __at a navigation system__, wherein the message contains a location reference and an advertising reference code; - assessing at least one advertisement associated with the advertising reference code __using the navigation system__; and - presenting the at least one advertisement to a user of the navigation system at a location based on the location reference code __using the navigation system__.

30. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 29 is implemented at client side of a traffic service network.

31. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 29 further comprising: - determining whether traffic data is present from message; - assessing a location description based, at least in part, on the location reference code; - assessing traffic data from the message associated with the location description; and - presenting the at least one advertisement along with the traffic data advertisement to a user of the navigation system.

32. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 29, wherein the at least one advertisement is any one or more selected from a group of an audio output, an video output, an icon output, and a text output.

33. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 29, wherein the message is broadcast using any one or more selected from a group of Radio Data System (RDS), Traffic Message Channel (TMC), Radio Data System-Traffic Message Channel (RDS-TMC), Vehicle Information and Communication System, digital radio, satellite radio, mobile Internet, mobile paging, and General Packet Radio Services/Global System for Mobile (GPRS/GSM) phone networks.

34. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 29, wherein the message uses any one or more selected from a group of an Alert-C protocol, Alert-Plus protocol, packet-based protocol, and Vehicle Information and Communication System message protocol.

35. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 29, wherein the location reference code comprises any one or more selected from a group of a geographic location, a point of interest, a local location of a geographic location.

36. (Previously presented) The method according to Claim 29, wherein the advertising reference code comprises any one or more selected from a group of resource codes representing at least a portion of an advertisement and a substantially unique code identifying at least a portion of an advertisement stored on a recipient device of the traffic message.

37. (Previously presented) A computer-readable medium having executable instructions stored thereon in accordance with the method of Claim 29.

38. (Previously presented) An apparatus having executable instructions stored thereon in accordance with the method of Claim 29.

39. (Previously presented) An apparatus of providing advertisements using location reference codes comprising: - a memory having a message with a location reference code and an advertising reference code; - an advertising provider coupled to the memory, wherein the advertising provider assesses at least one advertisement associated with the advertising reference code; and - a user interface coupled to the advertising provider, wherein the user interface provides the at least one advertisement associated with the advertising reference code for output on a navigation system.

40. (Previously presented) The apparatus according to Claim 39 further comprising: - a traffic reporter coupled to the user interface, wherein the traffic reporter assesses traffic information associated with the location reference code provided by the user interface.

41. (Previously presented) The apparatus according to Claim 39, wherein the advertising reference code comprises any one or more selected from a group of resource codes representing at least a portion of an advertisement and a substantially unique code identifying at least a portion of an advertisement stored on a recipient device of the traffic message.

42. (Currently amended) A __computer-readable__ memory comprising a data structure of traffic message, wherein the data structure comprises: a first field having a location reference code associated with a location description on a road segment assigned by a traffic message supplier; and a second field having an advertising reference code associated with the location reference of the first field, wherein the advertising reference code is associated with at least one advertisement for output on a navigation system.
